body.x: Nautilus Lab (CEO Eun-jeong Kim, www.nautilus-lab.com) unveiled its handwriting recognizing tablet series, the "Nautilus Note," at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The Nautilus Note comes with a stylish pen which supports pen pressure at the 2048 level. Its unique features include its memo application with a remarkable handwriting engine as well as its drawing application which provides a feeling as though one is actually writing on a notepad. The device comes in six different colors--pink, mint, green, yellow, gray, and metal--and writing appears in real time and as small in size as 0.3 mm and 0.5 mm.

Resolution of the Nautilus Note 10 is 1280 * 800 with an Android 4.4.4 (Kitkat) operating system and the device is equipped with a 10.1” IPS HD display. Other specs for the device includes a Quad-Core Cortex-A17, 1.8GHz processor with a 16GB memory with the option to select a 32GB or 64 GB memory. The front camera has a 2 million pixels lens while the rear camera shoots at 8 million pixels and the device is a light 561g. The Nautilus Note 8 comes with the same specs and resolution but with an 8” display and a mere 392g weight, making it an ideal proportion for users who are constantly on the move.
Nautilus Lab also plans to showcase a number of its handwriting-related applications including its Note App, Memo App, Sketchbook App, and Floating Memo App.
A spokesperson for Nautilus Lab enthused, “Through CES 2015, we plan to introduce our outstanding tablet PC and handwriting solution to buyers from all over the world.”

Nautilus Lab began in 2003 with its headquarters in Hong Kong focusing on educational device production and creation. The company currently supplies products and technical support in a wide range of regions around the world including Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Slovenia, Romania, and more.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.
